audit.whatIsWrong: The packet raised it as a defect in its own right: Vayne wins 39.28% over 2788 games, but the chart handed her five of seven stages.
audit.why: The mirror audit (malphite__vayne) resolved it the way the prose already argues — Vayne owns Levels 1-2 and the two-item stage, and Levels 3 through first item are Malphite's. That is the only reading consistent with a 39% win rate and with Ground Slam's flat 7s attack-speed cut arriving at level 3.
audit.corrected: phases[0]/win[0] to Vayne; phases[2]/win[2], phases[3]/win[3], phases[4]/win[4] and phases[5]/win[5] to Malphite; Levels 2 and 2+ items already read Vayne. All proposed as matched full/content pairs in one atomic group, with whys[2] through whys[5] rewritten so the prose and the chart tell the same story.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3], spikes[0] and mid all call Thunderclap his E. Thunderclap is W; E is Ground Slam.
audit.why: Getting the slot wrong hides the actual spike. Ground Slam (E) is a flat 7s at every rank that reduces attack speed — against a champion whose entire kit is attack-speed-based auto attacks, that is the ability that turns level 3 into his stage, and it was never mentioned once on the page. Thunderclap (W) is 10s falling to 8s, is an auto-attack reset, and applies on-hit, so his burst opens on an attack wind-up rather than a cast.
audit.corrected: Slot names fixed and Ground Slam's 7s attack-speed cut written into whys[2], whys[3], spikes[0], mid, wants.foe[1] and breakdown.cooldowns; the Thunderclap reset tell added to spikes[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and mid call Unstoppable Force 'a point-and-click knock-up you cannot dodge'; nothing on the page states what Granite Shield actually is.
audit.why: Riot's text: Malphite 'launches himself to a location at high speed' — it is a charge from 1000 range on 130s at rank 1, not a targeted cast, and it can miss. Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of his maximum health and only recharges if he has not been hit for a few seconds, which is the concrete reason continuous chip beats it and burst does not.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns now describe the charge with its range and cooldown; early is rewritten around Granite Shield's 10% cap and recharge condition.
